text: Rodney Brooks's 1991 paper 'Intelligence Without Representation' argued that:
choices: Intelligent behavior can emerge from direct sensorimotor coupling without internal world models, because 'the world is its own best model'
Richer and more detailed internal representations always yield more intelligent behavior
Symbolic logic is the only viable route to genuine machine intelligence
A robot must build a complete 3D map of its surroundings before it can act
explanation: Brooks challenged the representationalist assumption that getting the internal model right is the central problem of intelligence. His subsumption-architecture robots (Genghis, Allen, Herbert) produced surprisingly capable behavior from layered reactive rules with no world model. The other options restate exactly the planning-and-representation paradigm he was arguing against.
